newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dlr ends at 8-yr low on foreign speculation.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dlr ends at 8-yr low on foreign speculation.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed at an eight-year low against its U.S. counterpart on Tuesday following intense activities by overseas speculators to drive down the local currency, dealers said.
The local unit closed at T$27.921 against Monday's T$27.909 finish, marking its lowest level since hitting T$28.03 on January 7, 1989.
The T$27.921 close also surpassed the previous eight-year low of T$27.920 set on June 19.

Turnover was a hectic US$315.5 million -- T$41.5 million of which came in the last 15 minutes when the central bank, according to dealers, staunchly defended the local dollar to avert an even bigger slide.
Dealers said overseas speculation was heavy in the form of non-delivery forward trading.
"There are lots of activities involving NDFs, from investors seeking to intensify the Taiwan dollar's recent downtrend," said one dealer at a foreign bank.

Taiwan's currency has been on a slow decline since early 1997, with senior analysts polled by Reuters forecasting that the rate would slip to T$28 to the U.S. dollar in the second half -- but only when the central bank is ready.
"The central bank will not let the Taiwan dollar hit the T$28 level right away," said another dealer.
"But eventually the rate is acceptable because it will boost exports," she said.
A T$27.92-94 range was seen for Wednesday.
